topics.definition: NoSQL databases store and manage data using flexible data models instead of only relational tables.
tips: Choose the model that matches your data.

topics.definition: NoSQL databases provide flexibility, scalability and high availability.
SQL uses fixed schemas, while NoSQL supports flexible schemas.
Documents can have different structures without altering the database schema.
tips: Validate data at the application layer when needed.

topics.definition: NoSQL systems commonly scale by adding more servers.
tips: Use sharding for very large datasets.

topics.definition: NoSQL databases make trade-offs between consistency, availability and partition tolerance.
Popular NoSQL databases include MongoDB, Cassandra, Redis and Neo4j.
tips: Each database targets different use cases.

topics.definition: Design data models around application access patterns and monitor performance.
